title: A landmark on the way
hook: A familiar object can mark a place.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: In this toy map, food is next to the tree. If the animal uses that landmark, where should it search?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: In this toy map, food is next to the tree. If the animal uses that landmark, where should it search?

claims.text: In this toy map, food is next to the tree. If the animal uses that landmark, where should it search? The first panel places food beside the tree; the second shows the route toward the same landmark. A landmark can provide a spatial cue, but this stipulated example does not show that a real animal learned the route or which cues it used.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A toy food cache is placed beside a rock. Which landmark marks its location? In the stipulated example the rock identifies the food location.
